items.item: The grid header names the week with its date range (such as "Week 45 · 2–8 Nov 2026"), every day column shows the weekday and date, and controls move to the previous, next and current week
items.evidence: range-heading shows rangeLabel(weekStart) e.g. '1–7 Nov 2026'; each th shows d.weekdayShort ('Sun', 'Mon'...) plus d.date.getDate(); #prev-btn/#next-btn/#today-btn call addDays(weekStart,-7/7) and startOfWeek(TODAY). No explicit 'Week NN' number is shown, only the date range.

items.item: Each shift shows its start and end time in one consistent 24-hour format and the role or station (such as "07:00–15:00 · Cashier"), and a shift that ends after midnight is marked as ending the next day
items.evidence: fmtTime() uses Intl.DateTimeFormat(LOCALE,{hour:'numeric',minute:'2-digit'}) with LOCALE='en-US', rendering 12-hour times like '8 AM–4 PM' (visible in first.png), not 24-hour. The shift cell label is only `${fmtTime(start)}–${fmtTime(end)}` (renderWeekTable, line ~471) with no role/station in the cell — role only appears in a separate 'Role' column. No logic anywhere compares end<start or flags a next-day shift.

items.item: Each staff row shows the week's scheduled hours against contracted hours (such as "36 / 40 h"), the scheduled figure equals that person's shifts less unpaid breaks, and anyone over or under contract is flagged in words
items.evidence: STAFF objects only have {id,name,role} — no contracted-hours field exists anywhere in the script. The row's Hours cell renders only the summed total: `${hrs}` (e.g. '40', '32'), with no '/40h' comparison, no break deduction, and no over/under text flag.

items.item: A footer row shows, for each day, the staff count or hours scheduled against the required cover, and days below the requirement are marked in text (such as "Short 1")
items.evidence: week-foot-row renders `${count} of ${filteredStaff.length}` per day and, when count < MIN_STAFF (6), appends a text badge 'Below minimum' (renderWeekTable). Caveat: the displayed ratio is against total staff headcount (9), not the actual required-cover number (6), so the cover target itself is never shown to the user, only the shortfall label.

items.item: The sample data contains at least one rule conflict, such as overlapping shifts for one person or less than 11 hours' rest between a closing and the next opening shift, shown on the affected cell with a written reason
items.evidence: No conflict-detection code exists anywhere in the script (no overlap or rest-gap calculation). Checked the SHIFTS['2026-11-01'] data by hand: no staff member has two shifts on the same day, and the shortest close-to-open gap (e.g. s9 day4 ends 21:00, day5 starts 13:00) is 16h, well over 11h — the sample data contains no conflict at all.

items.item: Approved leave, days off and public holidays appear as labelled cells (such as "Annual leave", "Day off") that look different from an empty, unscheduled cell
items.evidence: Only one ad hoc category exists: UNAVAILABLE['2026-11-01'] has a single entry (s4, day 3, reason 'Requested day off') rendered as a dashed 'Unavailable' cell. There is no 'Annual leave' label, no public-holiday indicator, and 'Closed' cells represent the store being shut (day 0), not a staff day off — so leave/public-holiday categories called for by the checklist are absent.

items.item: The week's status (Draft or Published) is shown, and publishing goes through a confirmation that names the week and the number of unresolved conflicts or warnings
items.evidence: #status-badge shows 'Draft'/'Published' correctly (renderStatusBadge). But the publish confirm dialog text is `${shifts.length} shift(s) across ${staffCount} staff become visible to the team.` — it never names the week (no rangeLabel in the dialog, only used afterward in the toast) and never mentions unresolved conflicts/warnings, since no conflict detection exists at all.

items.item: The grid is a <table> with staff names as row headers and days as column headers, and each shift or empty cell is keyboard-reachable with an accessible name that includes the person and the date (such as "Add shift, Lan Pham, Tue 3 Nov")
items.evidence: Day headers are correctly ``, but the staff-name cell is rendered as a plain `...${staff.name}` — not a `` — so staff names are not semantic row headers. Cells are keyboard-reachable (`role="button" tabindex="0"` plus a keydown handler for Enter/Space) with aria-labels like 'Add shift for Ava Thompson, Sat 7 Nov 2026' that do include person and date.

items.item: A week with no shifts yet shows a message with a way to start (such as "Copy last week"), and a loading state and a load error with a retry button exist
items.evidence: The empty/first-use state (shifts.length===0) shows text 'Add shifts for the week, then publish it...' but its only action button is labelled 'Back to this week' (dataset.mode='today'), which just navigates to the current week rather than offering a way to start (e.g. copy last week) — no such feature exists in the script. The loading (data-state="loading" with #skeleton) and error (data-state="error" with #retry button) states do both exist correctly.

notes: Visually the page is restrained (audit score 100/100, no gradients/blur/uppercase tracked labels/emoji, radii 4-6px, single primary header action) and I found no clear template tells to flag. The failures are functional/data gaps rather than cosmetic: 12-hour time format instead of 24-hour, no contracted-hours tracking, no conflict/rest-rule detection, no leave/holiday taxonomy, missing row-header semantics, and a publish confirmation that omits the week name and warning count.
